gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Dogica is the loud one here, heavy and widely spaced, built to command attention. Noto Sans Syriac is the sans-serif that does the gentler work, its tall rounded bowls and easy s turns made for steady reading.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-syriac-ea: Dogica's lowercase climbs almost to capital height, and its wide tracking gives every heavy word plenty of room to stand. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern wants more size than you'd guess.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-syriac-we: Dogica is heavy, wide and unmistakably in charge. Shrink it and that wide spacing loosens, while enlarging Noto Syriac Western's plain sans body would make its thick little letters bulge like bundled cable.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Noto Sans Tagalog is a plain sans with a dense middle band. Dogica's wide, heavy capitals sit over it comfortably, and both fonts keep their curves generously open, which is what ties them together.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Dogica hits hard, heavy and widely tracked, with its lowercase reaching close to capital height. And Noto Sans Tagbanwa takes over once the shouting is done, a sans with open curves and lowercase filling most of the line.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Dogica's spacing is unusually wide, and its heavy letters never quite close their curves. Noto Sans Tai Le runs on gentle strokes that taper before touching, so a whole page of it moves along without friction.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri looks open and high-waisted, its small round letters left unclosed. Beneath Dogica's heavy, widely tracked lines, a full page of it would read lightly and without strain.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Dogica is heavy and widely spaced, with lowercase that nearly matches its capitals. Noto Sans Tamil is the sans-serif that looks magnified at any size, and its open terminals give the loud heading a spacious partner.
